chain: Pursuit of a sharper face and physique
clavicular-s-looksmaxxing-philosophy.text: Followers of streamer Clavicular treat his approach as a template for maximal 'ascension', combining drug protocols, bonesmashing talk and extreme self-improvement in pursuit of a more striking face and physique. The appearance claims come from his streams and anecdote rather than trials, and medical sources have criticised the approach.

chain: Post photos and get PSL ratings
Apply tips to face and body
looksmax-org-forum-participation.text: Members use the forum to post progress photos, request ratings and swap guides, treating the feedback and shared methods as a map for improving their looks. The feedback comes from peers on a self-devised rating scale, and the guides' methods vary from studied to anecdotal.

dopamine-porn-avoidance.text: Followers of NoFap and dopamine fasting abstain in the belief that it raises testosterone, focus and confidence, which they say make a person come across as more attractive. Researchers describe these specific appearance and hormone claims as unsupported, though dopamine fasting was developed as a behavioural tool.

chain: Adopt a dominant or lone-wolf identity
alpha-sigma-male-frameworks.text: Manosphere and looksmaxxing forum users sort men into alpha, beta and sigma types and adopt the high-status archetypes in the hope of seeming more attractive. The typology is borrowed from animal-behaviour research and is not an established model of human social life.

chain: Others read you as higher status
social-proof-status-maxxing.text: Users build visible signals such as followers, group photos and high-status associations to raise how attractive they seem. The psychology of social proof is well studied, while the looksmaxxing tactics built on it are untested.

chain: Offset or outweigh looks in dating
money-maxxing-career-maxxing.text: Looksmaxxing and manosphere communities present income and career success as a route to attractiveness, especially for men who see their looks as fixed. Mate-preference research partly supports a link between status and desirability, but the strategy itself has not been tested.

chain: Face looks warmer and more attractive
smile-practice-smile-maxxing.text: Users rehearse their smile in a mirror to look more genuine and symmetrical, drawing on the difference between polite and genuine smiles. Smile perception has been studied, but smile training itself has not.

posture-frame-body-language.text: Users hold an upright, open stance, sometimes as power posing, so they look taller and more confident while standing. The visual change is immediately visible; claims about hormone and behaviour shifts from posing have replicated poorly, though effects on how people feel are better supported.

chain: Spot which side or version looks better
photo-comparison-flip-test.text: Users flip photos or compare them with their mirror image to understand why they look different in pictures and to pick the more flattering version. It relates to the mere exposure effect, though the method itself has not been tested.

chain: Flip a face photo or split halves
mirror-flip-symmetry-test.text: Users reverse a face photo or compare its two halves to assess symmetry, one of several features in facial analysis. Symmetry features in attractiveness research, but this self-test has not been validated.

facial-analysis-youtube-channels.text: Viewers watch creators rate faces on feature scales such as PSL to learn which features to improve and how. The ratings are unvalidated, and press coverage links the content to body-image concerns.

anti-looksmax-touch-grass-critiques.text: Journalists, researchers and clinicians argue looksmaxxing can be harmful, while the informal 'touch grass' version urges absorbed users to go outside. Within the scene it is read as a counterweight to over-focus on looks, and the benefits it suggests are anecdotal.

therapy-for-looks-related-anxiety-act.text: Acceptance and commitment therapy is raised in looksmaxxing discussions as a way to handle appearance anxiety so it interferes less with daily life and social presence. ACT is well studied generally, though it has not been tested within looksmaxxing.

antidepressants-anxiety-meds.text: Prescription antidepressants and anxiety medicines are discussed in the scene as aids for social anxiety and low mood that can hold back confidence. They are prescribed for mental-health conditions rather than appearance, and an appearance benefit is anecdotal.

psychedelic-therapy-for-self-image.text: Some forum users float psilocybin, LSD or MDMA therapy as a way to reshape how they see their own appearance. Research has focused on depression, PTSD and anxiety, and no direct body-image studies exist.

social-media-dysmorphia-filter-dysmorphi.text: The term describes people who want to look like their filtered selfies, which drives interest in cosmetic procedures and in how photos are framed. Studies link filter use to body dissatisfaction and surgery interest, though it is an informal term and not a formal diagnosis.

beauty-privilege-research-pretty-premium.text: Looksmaxxers cite labour-economics findings that more attractive people tend to get better hiring and pay outcomes as a reason to invest in appearance. The premium is documented in research, while its size and causes are still debated.

chain: Targets for face and body changes
evolutionary-psychology-of-attractivenes.text: Looksmaxxers draw on evolutionary accounts of beauty to decide which features, such as symmetry and sexual dimorphism, to prioritise. Support in research is mixed and contested.

spreader-grafts.text: Surgeons place these cartilage strips during rhinoplasty to keep the middle of the nose straight and the bridge lines smooth after a hump is reduced. The reshaping is visible once healed; evidence consists mainly of surgeon case series.

columellar-strut-graft.text: Rhinoplasty patients get this concealed cartilage support to hold the nasal tip in a defined position. The change is visible after healing, though surgeons debate how much it raises the tip compared with septal extension grafts.

rib-cartilage-rhinoplasty.text: Surgeons use rib cartilage when septal cartilage is insufficient, mainly for major reconstruction and revision rhinoplasty that reshapes the nose. The result is visibly structural; evidence is limited to small surgeon series.

rhinoplasty-tip-narrowing-sutures.text: Rhinoplasty patients with a broad or bulbous tip get sutures that reshape the cartilage without removing it, giving a narrower tip. The change is visible after healing, and published support found here is sparse.

deep-plane-facelift.text: Facelift patients seek this technique to restore a tighter jawline, fuller midface and smoother neck in one repositioned layer. The lift is visible after healing; evidence is mostly surgeon series.

smas-plication-facelift.text: Patients choose this less invasive facelift for a moderate tightening of the lower face and jawline. The lift is visible after healing, with less mobilisation than deep plane or SMAS flap techniques.

chain: Midface and lower lid junction raised
composite-facelift.text: Facelift patients use this deep technique to lift sagging midface and smooth the lower eyelid to cheek junction for a more youthful look. The change is visible after healing; evidence is at surgeon-series level.

subperiosteal-facelift.text: Patients seek this midface lift, often done endoscopically, to raise sagging cheeks and soften deep nasolabial folds. The lift is visible after healing and is documented mainly in surgeon series from the 1990s onward.

mini-facelift-s-lift.text: Patients with deep nasolabial folds and sagging but a firm neck choose this short-scar lift for lighter downtime and a tighter lower face. The change is visible after healing, though Wikipedia describes the result as more temporary.

chain: Vertical lift of lower and midface
macs-lift.text: Patients choose this short-scar lift for a vertical lift of the lower and midface with quicker recovery under local anesthesia. The tightening is visible after healing, and recovery claims come from the authors' surgeon series.

aptos-thread-lift.text: Patients use these barbed threads as a non-surgical way to lift sagging facial tissue. Early series, including 186 patients, reported improved contour, while case reports describe thread migration and expulsion.

lower-facelift-with-neck-lift.text: Patients combine jowl lifting with platysma and fat work to define the jawline and neck together. The result is visible after healing; the literature is surgeon-reported with limited comparative data.
